note: The load-profile library. Drop a .json file in this folder and add it here to make it available — no code change. A browser cannot list a directory, so this manifest is what both the page and the desktop runner read.

schema.name: what a customer sees
schema.p: normalised power, +1 = peak discharge, negative = charge/regen
schema.note: what it represents and where it came from
schema.terrain: optional: tarmac | gravel | sand | mud | rock | snow

profiles.name: Daily solar cycle (charge midday, discharge evening)
City bus route (stop–go, heavy regen, layover)
RV / van day (cooking peaks, charging while driving)
Portable power box (appliance bursts, idle between)
AGV / lift truck shift (move–lift–return, opportunity charge)
Wearable gadget day (milliwatt base, burst peaks, dock charge)
Robot vacuum run (steady suction, dock recharge)
Full electric
profiles.description: The battery supplies the complete propulsion and auxiliary demand during the electric operating period.

profiles.name: Load levelling
profiles.description: Keep the genset at a stable set load: discharge the battery above it and charge below it.

profiles.name: Boost function
profiles.description: Add battery power above the propulsion system’s maximum continuous rating, then recharge at lower demand.

profiles.name: Spinning reserve
profiles.description: Hold the battery ready to take load immediately after a genset trip or sudden loss of generation.

profiles.name: Peak shaving
profiles.description: Cover sudden short peaks and bridge the time needed to start or ramp another generator.

profiles.name: Load smoothing
profiles.description: Filter rapid load fluctuations so the genset sees a steadier power demand.

profiles.name: Ramp support
profiles.description: Fill the genset response delay during fast demand ramps and absorb surplus while it ramps down.
